You analyze a geometric configuration. **No figure is given.** Only the coordinates below are available. The symbol names are neutral and carry no hint about their meaning.
# Objects to focus on (role binding)
Focus on the relation that holds among the following objects: {X1, X2, X3, X4}.
# Configuration
# The four common tangent lines of circles K1, K2 meet pairwise. The four MIXED intersections (one external + one internal tangent) are X1,X2,X3,X4; the two same-type intersections are He, Hi.
O1 = (-2.2849, -4.2209)
K1 = Circle(O1, 7.4607)
O2 = (10.1897, -0.5520)
K2 = Circle(O2, 3.6869)
X1 = (0.6526, 3.2154)
X2 = (7.3460, 3.1590)
X3 = (9.8079, -5.2117)
X4 = (4.2108, -8.8828)
He = (22.3772, 3.0324)
Hi = (6.0639, -1.7655)

# Premises (general, non-degenerate)
The two circles are disjoint and have four common tangents; the radii differ; the configuration is general (non-degenerate).
State the SINGLE most important invariant that ALWAYS holds for the general (non-special, non-degenerate) configuration, as a relation (concyclic / equal length / collinear / right angle). It must be non-trivial and follow from the structure. The answer is withheld.

ex.text: Each X_i forms a right angle with O1 and O2 (verified by zero dot product), confirming they lie on the circle with diameter O1O2.

For two disjoint circles, the four intersection points of their common tangents are concyclic. This is a classical result in geometry, known as the Miquel theorem for complete quadrilaterals. The circle passing through these four points (the Miquel circle) has its center at the midpoint of the segment joining the centers O1 and O2, and its diameter is the segment O1O2. This can be shown by considering the homothety centered at the external homothety center of the two circles, or by direct computation of the power of a point. Thus, X1, X2, X3, X4 always lie on this circle, regardless of the specific configuration.

But O1 and O2 are not collinear with Xi (else the circles would intersect), so O1 and O2 lie on opposite bisectors. Hence b is the line O1Xi and b' is O2Xi. (3) [Right angle at intersection of bisectors] Since b ⊥ b', we get ∠O1XiO2 = 90°. (4) [All four Xi lie on the same circle] The locus of points X satisfying ∠O1XO2 = 90° is the circle with diameter O1O2. Since Xi each satisfy this right‐angle, they are concyclic on that circle.

Step 3 (union of bisectors = perpendicular bisector): the two bisectors at X coincide in the two-line case, so O1X ⟂ ℓe and O2X ⟂ ℓi, hence ∠O1XO2 = 90°. Step 4 (power of a point): for any X on that circle with diameter O1O2, |XO1|² = |XO2|² = (|O1O2|/2)², so X lies on the circle. Therefore all four X1, X2, X3, X4 satisfy |XOi|² = (|O1O2|/2)², QED.
